title: What fair lending and UDAAP training do CFPB examiners expect?
description: What CFPB and FFIEC examiners expect of fair lending and UDAAP training in a compliance management system, and the 2025 to 2026 changes, as at November 2026.
shortAnswer: Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) examiners assess training as one element of an institution's compliance management system. The CFPB Supervision and Examination Manual expects comprehensive, timely training tailored to each role, covering prohibitions against unlawful discrimination and unfair, deceptive, or abusive acts or practices (UDAAP), delivered to staff, audit personnel and relevant service providers, updated before new products or rules take effect, and documented with schedules, materials and completion records.
keyTakeaways: The CFPB's compliance management review procedures (August 2017) list training inside the Compliance Program, one of two interdependent CMS control components alongside Board and Management Oversight.
Requirements on unlawful discrimination and UDAAP "should be incorporated into training for all relevant officers and employees, including audit personnel."

Examiners request board and senior management training records, sample materials including fair lending and marketing scripts, records of follow-up on units below completion targets, and the 12 month training plan.
The FFIEC Uniform Interagency Consumer Compliance Rating System, effective March 31, 2017, rates training as an assessment factor for all supervised institutions, not only those the CFPB examines.

As at November 2026 the CFPB has withdrawn much guidance (May 12, 2025) and amended Regulation B to remove the disparate-impact "effects test" (effective July 21, 2026); the CMS training expectations themselves are unchanged.
regulator: Consumer Financial Protection Bureau (CFPB) for banks and credit unions over $10 billion and supervised nonbanks; the prudential regulators (OCC, FDIC, Federal Reserve, NCUA) for smaller institutions, using the FFIEC Uniform Interagency Consumer Compliance Rating System
appliesTo: Insured depository institutions and credit unions with total assets over $10 billion, and their affiliates (12 U.S.C. 5515)
Nonbank providers of consumer financial products that the CFPB supervises
Smaller banks and credit unions, examined for consumer compliance by their prudential regulator
Service providers with consumer contact or compliance responsibilities

sections.heading: Where do fair lending and UDAAP training expectations come from?

blocks.text: They come from supervisory expectations for a compliance management system (CMS), not from a rule that mandates a course. The substantive laws, the Equal Credit Opportunity Act (ECOA) and its Regulation B, and the Dodd-Frank Act's UDAAP prohibitions in 12 U.S.C. 5531 and 5536, say what institutions must not do. The CFPB's [compliance management review examination procedures](https://files.consumerfinance.gov/f/documents/201708_cfpb_compliance-management-review_supervision-and-examination-manual.pdf), part of its Supervision and Examination Manual, say how examiners check that staff know it.

The procedures describe a CMS as how an institution establishes its compliance responsibilities, "communicates those responsibilities to employees", builds them into business processes, reviews operations and takes corrective action. An effective CMS has two interdependent control components: Board and Management Oversight, and a Compliance Program made up of policies and procedures, training, monitoring and/or audit, and consumer complaint response.

The CFPB has exclusive examination authority over insured banks and credit unions with more than $10 billion in assets under [12 U.S.C. 5515](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/USCODE-2024-title12/html/USCODE-2024-title12-chap53-subchapV-partB-sec5515.htm); smaller institutions are examined by their prudential regulator. Both groups are rated under the same interagency framework, described below.

sections.heading: What does the CFPB Supervision and Examination Manual say about training?

blocks.text: The manual says education of the board, management and staff is essential to an effective compliance program, and that discrimination and UDAAP prohibitions belong in training for every relevant officer and employee, including auditors.

blocks.title: CFPB Compliance Management Review procedures, Training objectives
blocks.text: "Requirements for compliance with Federal consumer financial laws, including prohibitions against unlawful discrimination and unfair, deceptive, and abusive acts and practices, should be incorporated into training for all relevant officers and employees, including audit personnel."
Examiners are directed to determine whether:

items: Compliance training is comprehensive, timely, and specifically tailored to the particular responsibilities of the staff receiving it, including those responsible for product development, marketing and customer service.
The training program is updated proactively in advance of the rollout of new or changed products or the effective date of new or changed consumer protection laws and regulations.
Training is consistent with, and designed to reinforce, policies and procedures.
Compliance professionals have access to the training they need to run a program tailored to the entity's risk profile, business strategy and operations.

blocks.text: Board members are held to a different standard: they "should receive sufficient information to enable them to understand the entity's responsibilities and the commensurate resource requirements." Management and staff should receive specific, comprehensive training that reinforces written policies and procedures.

sections.heading: What will examiners ask to see?

blocks.text: The examination procedures list ten steps for the training review, most of which are document requests. In practice an institution should be able to produce the following on request:

items: The schedule, completion records and materials for recent compliance training of board members and senior management.
Evidence of the compliance officer's involvement in selecting, reviewing or delivering training content.

Policies, schedules and completion records for compliance professionals, managers and staff, and documents showing that service providers with consumer contact or compliance responsibilities are appropriately trained.
Samples of training content on fair lending, new or changed regulatory requirements, new or changed products or distribution channels, and marketing, "including scripts".
Training created to fulfill management commitments arising from monitoring, audit or examination findings, or from consumer complaints.

Sales practices training covering ethical standards and reporting of improper behavior, common risky behaviors, accurate description of terms and conditions, and evidence of consumer consent for account opening and upselling.
Records of follow-up, escalation and enforcement for units whose completion rates miss the institution's own standards or deadlines.
The plan for training changes over the next 12 months, which examiners compare with what was actually delivered against prior plans.

blocks.text: The final step is a preliminary conclusion that the training program is strong, satisfactory, deficient, seriously deficient or critically deficient. The sales practices step is where UDAAP risk most often surfaces, because production incentives and unauthorized account openings are classic sources of unfair or abusive practices.

sections.heading: How does the FFIEC rating system treat training at smaller institutions?

blocks.text: Training is a named assessment factor in the [Uniform Interagency Consumer Compliance Rating System](https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2016/11/14/2016-27226/uniform-interagency-consumer-compliance-rating-system), adopted by the Federal Financial Institutions Examination Council (FFIEC) agencies and effective March 31, 2017 (81 FR 79473). The system applies to banks and credit unions of every size, so a community bank examined by the FDIC or a credit union examined by the NCUA faces the same training factor as a large bank examined by the CFPB.

The rating system has three categories: Board and Management Oversight, Compliance Program, and Violations of Law and Consumer Harm. Training sits under Compliance Program, with descriptions running from training that is "comprehensive, timely, and specifically tailored" at the top rating to training that is "critically absent" at the bottom. In responding to comments, the agencies said the factor already expects compliance training programs to "encompass consumer protection laws and regulations", including fair lending, and declined to add more specificity. Expectations scale with size, complexity and risk, but the agencies state that all institutions, regardless of size, should maintain an effective CMS.

sections.heading: What changed for fair lending and UDAAP in 2025 and 2026?

blocks.text: The CFPB narrowed several interpretive positions but did not change the CMS training framework. Training content, rather than training structure, is what needs updating.

blocks.caption: Selected CFPB actions affecting fair lending and UDAAP training content (as at November 2026)

rows: Withdrawal of interpretive rules, policy statements and advisory opinions (90 FR 20084)
Training that cited withdrawn CFPB guidance documents as authority should be reviewed and re-sourced to statutes, regulations or current guidance

Regulation B no longer refers to the "effects test" and now states the Act does not recognize it; fair lending modules built around disparate-impact analysis under Regulation B need revision
Definitions of unfair and abusive practices remain the core of UDAAP training

blocks.title: Status note
blocks.text: The Regulation B change reflects the CFPB's reading of ECOA. Other fair lending laws and other regulators' positions are outside this page, and institutions should take legal advice before removing content. The CMS examination procedures cited here are dated August 2017 and remained the CFPB's published procedures as at November 2026.

sections.heading: What UDAAP standards should training actually teach?

blocks.text: Staff need the statutory tests, applied to their own products and scripts. Under [12 U.S.C. 5531(c)](https://www.govinfo.gov/content/pkg/USCODE-2024-title12/html/USCODE-2024-title12-chap53-subchapV-partC-sec5531.htm), an act or practice is unfair only if it causes or is likely to cause substantial injury to consumers that is not reasonably avoidable by consumers and is not outweighed by countervailing benefits to consumers or to competition.

Under 5531(d), an act or practice is abusive if it materially interferes with a consumer's ability to understand a term or condition, or takes unreasonable advantage of a consumer's lack of understanding of material risks, costs or conditions, inability to protect their own interests, or reasonable reliance on the provider to act in their interests. Teaching these tests through the institution's real marketing copy, call scripts and fee practices is what the manual's request for "marketing (including scripts)" training samples is testing.

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry maps each consumer protection requirement, product and script to the roles that handle it, so fair lending and UDAAP learning outcomes are defined per role before content is written. When a rule such as Regulation B changes, the framework shows every outcome, module and assessment that relied on the old text, which is the proactive update examiners look for.

faqs.q: Does the CFPB require annual fair lending training?
faqs.a: The CFPB's procedures do not set a fixed frequency. They ask whether training is comprehensive, timely and tailored, updated before product or rule changes, and delivered according to the institution's own schedule and 12 month plan, with follow-up where units miss completion deadlines. Many institutions choose annual training as their baseline.

faqs.q: Do auditors need fair lending and UDAAP training?
faqs.a: Yes. The CFPB procedures state that requirements on unlawful discrimination and UDAAP should be incorporated into training for all relevant officers and employees, "including audit personnel", since auditors test the compliance program and need to recognize violations.

faqs.q: Are vendors covered by CFPB training expectations?
faqs.a: Yes, where they have consumer contact or compliance responsibilities. Examiners request documents showing such service providers are appropriately trained, and the service provider oversight procedures ask whether the institution ensures the provider trains and oversees its employees or agents.

faqs.q: Does the 2026 Regulation B change remove the need for fair lending training?
faqs.a: No. The final rule effective July 21, 2026 removed the effects test from Regulation B, but ECOA's prohibitions on discrimination and discouragement remain, as do the CFPB and FFIEC expectations that compliance training cover fair lending. The content of training changes; the obligation to train does not.
